title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A pleasantly mixed bag this time: free holiday rides in west Charlotte, a road fix on the way in St James, schoolboy football drama in Jamaica, and a sweet origin story about OutKast's very first hit. There's also some bigger-picture news out of Washington about Congress and oversight, plus a tidy reminder to keep lithium batteries out of your shredding pile.

stories.headline: Hidden battery sparks fire at Huntersville shred event
stories.summary: A Huntersville Police document-shredding event on Saturday got some unexpected excitement when a fire broke out inside the shred truck. Firefighters suspect a lithium battery tucked into the donated papers was to blame. No injuries were reported in the coverage.
key_facts: Event held in the 9600 block of Julian Clark Avenue, Huntersville
Hosted by Huntersville Police to help residents prevent identity theft
Suspected cause: a lithium battery mixed in with shred donations
stories.why: A handy reminder to check your paper piles for stray batteries before dropping them off for shredding or recycling.

links.title: Lithium battery sparks fire at Huntersville paper shredding event

stories.headline: Kingston College rallies into Champions Cup semis
stories.summary: Kingston College came from a goal down to beat first-time participants Denbigh High 2-1 on Saturday, completing the ISSA Champions Cup semi-final lineup. Deshawn Byfield scored both goals for the two-time champions. Denbigh's Lashawn Barnaby had several chances to level things up but couldn't find the net again.
key_facts: Final score: Kingston College 2, Denbigh High 1
Deshawn Byfield scored in the 27th and 57th minutes
KC will face Mona High in the semis, their third meeting this season
Glenmuir High will meet Wolmer's Boys in the other semi-final
stories.why: A classic comeback, and a rubber-match semi-final against Mona High to look forward to.

links.title: KC beat Denbigh to advance to Champions Cup semis

stories.headline: Trump order tells contractors to check with White House before answering Congress
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order Friday directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult the administration about congressional inquiries and to withhold communications the White House considers privileged. Contractors who don't comply could lose their contracts. The move comes ahead of Democrats taking control of Congress in January, when they plan investigations including into government contracts.
key_facts: Order is titled "Protecting the Executive's Privileges and Enhancing Efficiencies in Federal Contracting"
It applies to all federal contractors and subcontractors, tens of thousands of companies
Rep. Robert Garcia, top Democrat on House Oversight, called it an attack on Congress's oversight role
The White House says it protects executive privilege from "congressional overreach"
stories.why: Executive privilege isn't absolute, so this could set up lengthy legal fights over how much Congress can investigate in the coming term.

stories.headline: Smoother roads coming between Reading and Great River
stories.summary: Drivers in St James, Jamaica, should start feeling some relief as paving gets underway on the Reading to Great River corridor. The National Works Agency says 400 metres of asphalt were set to be finished Saturday, with crews then heading toward Reading. Traffic snarls during the works have frustrated drivers, including those handling visitor transfers.
key_facts: Part of the J$400 million SPARK road programme
400 metres of roadway paved near the Great River bridge
Completion expected in March 2027
stories.why: Light at the end of the traffic tunnel for commuters and tourism drivers in the area.

links.title: Relief coming for drivers along Reading to Great River corridor

stories.headline: Kingston launches its first marlin tournament
stories.summary: The inaugural Mayberry/Royal Jamaica Yacht Club Marlin Tournament got underway this week, with a Captain's Briefing Thursday and two days of fishing Friday and Saturday. Mayberry Investments is title sponsor, extending its long support of Jamaican sport fishing to Kingston's own waters.
key_facts: Mayberry committed J$2 million as title sponsor
Held at the RJYC at Palisadoes
Mayberry also sponsors the Superstars of Port Antonio tournament, which held its ninth staging in October
stories.why: A brand-new sporting tradition for the south coast, and as the sponsor put it, fishing rewards patience.

links.title: Inaugural Mayberry/RJYC Marlin Tournament sets sail

stories.headline: Yes, even your fridge needs cybersecurity
stories.summary: After hackers remotely raised fridge temperatures at supermarkets across Europe, a Jamaican cybersecurity expert is urging people and businesses to think about all their connected devices, not just computers. Jevon Davis of Guardsman Cyber Intelligence says some attackers just want to cause disruption, not steal money.
key_facts: The European attacks hit over 700 stores, causing millions of euros in losses
Affected France in October and around seven other European companies in November
Davis advises keeping an inventory of connected equipment and knowing who manages it
stories.why: A simple, practical step: know which of your gadgets are online and who can access them.

links.title: Why cybersecurity matters from your phone to your fridge

stories.headline: Big Boi on how OutKast turned a Christmas gig into a classic
stories.summary: On his podcast with his sons, Big Boi recalled OutKast being passed over twice before finally getting a single slot, on a holiday compilation, which felt to him like being set up to fail. Instead of a typical Christmas song, he and André 3000 wrote about hanging out at the Dungeon studio, and the track became "Player's Ball." The label later removed the sleigh bells so it could keep playing after the holidays.
key_facts: Original working title: "Socks and Drawers"
RCA dates the release to November 19, 1993
It topped the rap chart and helped launch their 1994 debut album
OutKast entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2025
stories.why: A feel-good reminder that a "no" (or an awkward assignment) can turn into something great.

links.title: Big Boi Revisits The Two Rejections Before OutKast’s Christmas Breakthrough

stories.headline: Eminem's publishers add 108 examples to AI music lawsuit
stories.summary: Eight Mile Style and Martin Affiliated amended their federal lawsuit against AI music platform Suno, adding 108 examples of tracks they say copied lyrics or music from 26 Eminem-related works. They say this challenges Suno's claim that users can't request specific artists or songs.
key_facts: Amended complaint filed November 19 in the Northern District of California
Original suit filed November 6, covering 269 compositions
Publishers seek up to $40.35 million in statutory damages
Eminem himself is not a plaintiff
disputed: The infringement claims are allegations; nothing has been decided by a court.
Suno says it makes original music and has never allowed prompts for specific artists or copyrighted songs.
stories.why: It's one of the cases that could shape how AI music tools are allowed to work.

links.title: Eminem’s Publishers Add 108 Examples To Suno Copyright Lawsuit
